title: Departments of a Commercial Organisation
tagline: The seven departments the syllabus names — purchase, production, marketing, finance, human resources, administration and legal — their functions and their interrelationships.

sourceNote.boardprep: Original BoardPrep study material written against the CISCE ICSE Commercial Applications syllabus registered in this subject’s baseline (Examination Year 2027 and 2028 documents as reproduced by AglaSem, Scribd and Oswal Publishers; cisce.org returned 403). No board examination paper was consulted, every question is original practice, no figure is presented as an official statistic, and — as the syllabus itself requires — no question asks the student to record accounting entries or perform accounting calculations.

overview.intro: Unit 2 is a study of how a firm is put together. The syllabus names seven departments — Purchase and Stores, Production, Marketing and Sales, Finance, Human Resources, General Administration and Legal — and asks for their roles, their interrelationships and their mutual dependence, studied through case studies or projects. Interrelationship is the operative word: the marks lie in showing that no department succeeds alone, so this chapter teaches each department’s function first, then follows one order end to end across all seven, and finally examines a case where the departments must negotiate a conflict. The through-line is that departments divide work, not responsibility — every product sold is the joint output of all seven.

learningOutcomes: State the function of each of the seven departments.
Explain the interrelationship between any two named departments.
Trace a single order through all seven departments.
Identify the department responsible for a given business problem.
Use a case study to show mutual dependence between departments.

learn.title: The seven functions: what each department does

blocks.text: Purchase and Stores secures everything the firm consumes — raw material, spares, tools and office supplies — by identifying suppliers, negotiating prices and quality, placing orders, and receiving and holding the goods in the store until issued. Production converts those inputs into finished goods on schedule, controlling machines, methods, quality and output volume. Marketing and Sales finds what customers want, prices it, persuades buyers through selling and advertising, and takes the orders; without it, production has no direction and no revenue. Finance raises the money the firm runs on, keeps the books, plans expenditure, collects receivables and reports how the firm is doing — every other department spends what Finance releases. Human Resources recruits, trains, appraises and pays people, and handles discipline and welfare, so it supplies the skill on which all six others depend. General Administration coordinates: it keeps communication flowing, maintains premises and records, arranges meetings and implements the policies that make six departments behave like one firm. Legal advises and protects — drafting contracts, defending the firm’s rights, ensuring the business stays inside the law. Each definition should be learned with a verb, because a department’s function is always something it does for the others.

learn.title: Interrelationships: why no department stands alone

blocks.text: The syllabus asks for interrelationships and dependence, and the cleanest way to show them is to follow one thread. A purchase order exists because Marketing forecast demand; the goods are bought only because Production can use them, and on terms only Finance can accept. Stores issues material to Production, which returns finished goods that Stores again holds until Marketing sells them. Marketing cannot promise delivery without knowing Production’s capacity, and Production cannot schedule without knowing Marketing’s orders — the same information moving in a loop. Finance depends on Sales for cash and on every department for the cost figures that make a profit possible; in return it sets the budget within which each must work. Human Resources hires when Production expands and trains when a new machine arrives. Legal is engaged whenever Purchase signs a supplier contract or Marketing signs a distributor. Administration holds the loop together by scheduling the meetings where these dependencies are reconciled. The typical examination answer names two departments and shows the two-way flow — purchase and production, or marketing and production — because dependence is rarely one-directional: each party supplies something the other needs.

learn.title: One order, seven departments: the cycle end to end

blocks.text: A single order exercises the whole organisation. It begins with Marketing and Sales receiving an order for a thousand cartons and passing the requirement inward. Finance checks the customer’s credit and releases the funds the purchase will need. Purchase and Stores places the material order, receives the goods, inspects them and puts them in the store. Production draws the material, schedules the run, manufactures the cartons and passes quality control, reporting finished stock back to Stores. Human Resources has already staffed and trained the line and now handles the overtime that the deadline requires. Legal has vetted the supply contract and the terms offered to the customer, ensuring the firm is not carrying unlimited risk. General Administration coordinates the whole cycle — circulating the schedule, keeping the records and calling the review meeting when delivery is threatened. Finance closes the loop by invoicing the customer, recording the receipts and costing the order so the firm knows whether the thousand cartons actually earned anything. The cycle is the syllabus’s case-study method in miniature, and the exam answer that scores is the one that names each department’s specific act, not merely that it was involved.

items: Marketing → order; Finance → credit clearance; Purchase → material.
Production → goods; Stores → stock records; Human Resources → the people and the overtime.
Legal → compliant terms; Administration → coordination; Finance again → invoice and cost.
If any one step stalls, the whole cycle stalls — that is the meaning of mutual dependence.

learn.title: The case-study method: diagnosing a breakdown

blocks.text: The syllabus prescribes case studies or projects, so students should practise the diagnostic form. Take a firm whose delivery dates slip regularly. The surface complaint sits with Marketing, whose promises are late; the first examination checks Production, where machine breakdowns and unplanned rework consume days; behind that sits Purchase, which has been buying cheaper components that fail incoming inspection; behind that sits Finance, which approved the cheaper supplier’s terms to protect margins; and underneath all of it sits Human Resources, which never scheduled preventive maintenance because the maintenance role was left unfilled. Administration failed to surface the conflict because the departments reported separately. A strong answer refuses to blame one department: it names the chain, states which department owns each link, and proposes the fix at each level — qualified supplier list, planned maintenance, a standing cross-department review chaired by administration. This is how the syllabus wants the topic examined: not “list the departments” but “show what happens when their interrelationship fails”. Students should be able to run this analysis in both directions — from symptom back to cause, and from a proposed change forward to its effects on the other six.

keyPoints: The syllabus names seven departments: purchase and stores, production, marketing and sales, finance, human resources, administration and legal.
Purchase buys and stores; Production converts; Marketing sells; Finance funds.
Human Resources supplies the people every other department needs.
General Administration coordinates communication, records and policy.
Legal protects the firm through contracts and compliance.
Interrelationship means each department’s output becomes another’s input.
The classic two-way pairs are purchase–production and marketing–production.
A single order exercises all seven departments from forecast to receipt.
The syllabus prescribes case studies or projects, so diagnosis matters more than listing.
When one department fails, the failure propagates — mutual dependence cuts both ways.
examFocus: “Describe the functions of the departments” — one function verb plus one concrete act per department.
“Explain the interrelationship between marketing and production” — a two-way answer: orders and forecasts one way, capacity and delivery dates the other.
Case-study question — identify each department’s link in the chain and give a remedy at every link, not a single blame.

vocabulary.meaning: A specialised unit of a firm responsible for one group of activities.
The two-way dependence between departments, where each supplies what the other needs.
The department that buys material and holds it in the store until issued.
Funds needed for day-to-day operations — released by Finance to keep every department running.
The activity of aligning departments’ plans so the firm acts as one.
Operating within the law, ensured by the Legal department.

The assessment of an employee’s performance, conducted by Human Resources.

questions.prompt: The department that raises funds, keeps the books and plans expenditure is:
questions.explanation: Finance arranges the firm’s money — raising it, budgeting it, recording it and collecting receivables — while the other departments spend what Finance releases.
questions.commonMistake: Accounts are recorded by Finance, not by General Administration, which only coordinates.

questions.prompt: Production cannot schedule work without information from which department?
questions.explanation: Marketing passes orders and demand forecasts inward; without them Production does not know what, how much or when to make.
questions.commonMistake: Human Resources supplies workers, but the schedule itself comes from demand.

questions.prompt: A supplier contract must be vetted before signing. The department that advises on it is:
questions.explanation: Legal drafts and checks contracts so the firm’s rights and risks are clear before any party is bound.
questions.commonMistake: Finance approves the money terms; Legal approves the enforceable terms — both are involved.

questions.prompt: A firm keeps buying cheaper components that repeatedly fail inspection. Which department’s decision is primarily at fault?
questions.explanation: Purchase chooses suppliers and terms, so accepting substandard components is a purchasing decision; quality criteria should be part of every purchase order it raises.
questions.commonMistake: The failure appears in Production, but the cause sits where the supplier was selected.

questions.prompt: The department that recruits, trains and pays employees is ______.
questions.explanation: Human Resources handles staffing end to end — selection, training, appraisal, wages and welfare — supplying the skill every other department runs on.
questions.commonMistake: General Administration does not staff roles; it coordinates the people already in them.

questions.prompt: State any three functions of the Purchase and Stores department.
questions.answer: It identifies and evaluates suppliers and places orders for the material the firm needs; it inspects incoming goods for quantity and quality before accepting them; and it holds the material in the store, maintains stock records and issues it to production on requisition.
questions.explanation: The three functions cover buying, checking and holding, which together explain why the department is called Purchase and Stores rather than Purchase alone.
questions.commonMistake: Do not mention selling — that belongs to Marketing and Sales.

questions.prompt: Explain the interrelationship between Finance and the other departments.
questions.answer: Finance depends on the other departments for figures: Purchase reports what material cost, Production reports the cost of making, and Marketing reports the revenue earned from sales. In return, Finance releases the budget each department spends, sets credit terms, and collects and records payments. The relationship is therefore two-way — every department feeds Finance the numbers it needs to report profit, and Finance feeds every department the funds it needs to operate.
questions.explanation: Both directions are stated with concrete flows, which is what “interrelationship” requires; a one-way answer shows dependence but not relationship.
questions.commonMistake: Do not describe Finance as merely a record-keeper; the release of funds is the other half of the relationship.

questions.prompt: Trace a customer order through all the departments of a commercial organisation, showing what each department contributes.
questions.answer: Marketing and Sales receives the order and passes the requirement inward. Finance checks the customer’s credit and releases the funds needed to execute it. Purchase and Stores orders the material, inspects it on arrival and holds it in the store. Production draws the material, schedules the run, manufactures the goods and passes them through quality control, reporting finished stock to Stores. Human Resources ensures the line is staffed and trained and approves any overtime the deadline demands. Legal vets the terms offered to the customer and the contracts with suppliers so the firm carries no unbounded risk. General Administration coordinates the schedule, keeps the records and convenes the review when delivery is threatened. Finance then invoices the customer, records receipt and costs the order to establish whether it earned a profit. Every department therefore touches the same order, and a delay in any one of them delays delivery.
questions.explanation: The answer moves in the order the business actually moves, naming a specific act for each of the seven departments and closing with the cost of failure — the interrelationship the unit tests.
questions.commonMistake: Do not omit Legal or Administration because they do not handle the goods; their acts are part of the cycle.

questions.prompt: Why does the syllabus ask students to study departments through case studies or projects? Illustrate your answer with one case.
questions.answer: Because a list of functions shows what each department does, but a case shows how they depend on each other — the syllabus’s second requirement. In a case, a firm’s soap sells faster than it can be produced: Marketing won the campaign, but Production had no spare capacity, Purchase had not secured additional raw material, Finance had not approved the working-capital increase, and Human Resources had not hired for the additional shift. Administration never called a meeting at which the conflict could surface. The case reveals what the list cannot: each department was individually competent yet the firm failed, because the interrelationships were not managed. Studying cases also trains diagnosis — identifying which link in the chain broke and where the remedy belongs — which is the skill an examiner rewards when a problem is presented for analysis.
questions.explanation: The answer explains the pedagogical reason first, then uses a complete case covering all seven departments to show the failure of a link, which demonstrates rather than asserts the method’s value.
questions.commonMistake: Do not only narrate a case; the question first asks why the method is prescribed.

questions.prompt: A company’s deliveries are late for six months. Using the seven departments, analyse the possible causes at each level and propose a coordinated remedy.
questions.answer: Marketing may be at fault for promising dates without confirming production capacity, so commitments outrun reality. Production may be absorbing machine breakdowns and rework, which points to deferred maintenance and weak in-line quality checks. Purchase may be supplying components that fail inspection, forcing production to wait or rework. Finance may have withheld funds for spares or overtime to protect margins, creating the delay that Purchase and Production then inherit. Human Resources may have left technical posts unfilled, so neither maintenance nor quality inspection is adequately staffed. Legal may have signed supplier contracts without delivery clauses, removing any remedy when suppliers are late. General Administration may be the deepest cause, since no standing coordination forum existed to surface any of these conflicts before they accumulated. The coordinated remedy works at every level: Marketing confirms dates through a production-planning check; Production adopts planned maintenance and in-line inspection; Purchase applies an approved supplier list with quality and delivery clauses; Finance releases a maintenance and overtime budget; Human Resources fills the technical posts; Legal adds enforceable delivery terms; and Administration chairs a weekly cross-department review that reports on all six. The remedy is coordinated because fixing one link while leaving the others restores the delay elsewhere.
questions.explanation: Every department receives a diagnosis and a remedy, and the closing reasoning explains why a single-point fix fails — the mutual dependence the unit is built to teach.
questions.commonMistake: Blaming Production alone is the classic error: the question names seven departments for a reason.
